requirement.title: Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code

acceptance_criteria.text: Every type emitted by the source generator carries [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage].
acceptance_criteria.status: supported without a passing linked test

acceptance_criteria.text: The feature applies to every consumer target where the attribute exists.
Generated code still compiles for every existing valid user project.

acceptance_criteria.status: supported without a passing linked test

claims.text: All generated formatters and resolvers are decorated with [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage].
The attribute is only emitted for targets where it is available (not netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework).
Tests verify that every generated type is excluded and that the attribute is guarded.

zones.why: Frozen generator output; checkable by a mechanical rule derived from the requirement.
Tests are evidence; their strength is measured, not assumed.
Changes the code compiled into every user's projects.
Code produced by T4 from the .tt; its observable behaviour is the generated output (snapshots). Read the .tt, not the .cs.
Documentation; read because it makes claims.

evidence.what: Full MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests suite on the branch (regenerates every snapshot and compares it with the committed file)
evidence.note: The snapshots were regenerated by the agent: the suite proves consistency with the new snapshots, not the absence of a behaviour change.

evidence.detail: 2/2 fail on base, 2/2 pass on the branch

evidence.what: Does a user who already has [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] on their partial resolver still compile?
evidence.detail: Base: compiles. Branch: error CS0579: Duplicate 'global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage' attribute (MyNs.MyResolver.g.cs(13,2))

evidence.what: Is code written by hand in a user's partial resolver excluded from coverage?
evidence.detail: Base: not excluded. Branch: MyNs.MyResolver carries the attribute → the user-written method UserWrittenLogic is excluded from coverage

evidence.what: Does ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute exist in netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework?
evidence.detail: Present in netstandard.library 2.0.3 ref/netstandard.dll and in .NETFramework v4.7.2 System.dll

refusals.question: Should the feature be shipped to netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework consumers?
refusals.why: The agent's restriction rests on a false premise; widening it changes the delivered scope

evidence.what: Do all types emitted by the generator carry the attribute?
evidence.detail: Every generated type carries the attribute (directly or through another partial declaration). 3 snapshots without the attribute: folder Resources/InterfaceUnion, unchanged and referenced by no test (pre-existing dead fixture).

Only checks that each generated file contains the attribute string at least once (text.Contains) and that each occurrence is wrapped in the #if. Does not check each type, does not compile a user project, and encodes C2's false assumption as expected behaviour.

evidence.by: E2E sandbox (real consumer project, net8.0 + netstandard2.0, inspected by reflection)
evidence.what: A real user project built with the generator: which types are excluded from coverage, per target?
evidence.detail: net8.0: 5 generated types excluded (OK) BUT AppResolver.UserBusinessRule, written by the user, is excluded too. netstandard2.0: no type excluded → feature missing although the attribute exists (E5).
evidence.artifacts: factory/e2e/Consumer, factory/e2e/Runner (console output kept in the passport)

refusals.question: Should code written by hand in a user's partial resolver be excluded from coverage?
refusals.why: Visible effect in users' coverage reports; the requirement does not say so

evidence.by: Diff-scoped mutation testing (revert one hunk at a time)
evidence.what: Do the tests notice each of the agent's changes?
evidence.detail: Tests delivered by the agent: 3/10 mutants killed. Full suite: 10/10 (thanks to the snapshots, which detect any output change without saying whether it is correct).

evidence.by: Catching tests generated from the criteria (claude -p --model sonnet), without seeing the agent's tests or ours
evidence.what: 8 disposable scenarios run on base and branch
evidence.detail: 1 catch: C5_AC_3_UserResolverAlreadyAnnotated passes on base, fails on the branch ([] MessagePack.SourceGenerator/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator/App.MyResolver.g.cs(13,2): error CS0579: Duplicate 'global::System.Diagnostics.C). Rediscovers E3 independently. 3 scenarios with no difference, 4 fail on both sides (see E11).

evidence.by: Catching tests — failures on both sides, reviewed
evidence.what: Scenarios that fail on base AND branch: criterion not met or invalid test?
evidence.detail: C1/C2/C3: the wrapper class generated for the namespace (e.g. App.MyResolver.App) does not carry the attribute; it is only covered through its parent class. C8: invalid test (wrong expected bytes, also fails on base) — discarded.

refusals.question: Is a nested generated class, excluded only through its parent class, enough for the targeted coverage tools?
refusals.why: Depends on the coverage tool's behaviour (attribute inheritance to nested types); not specified by the issue

evidence.what: Assertion strength and test → criterion links across 12 tests
evidence.detail: AllGeneratedTypesAreExcludedFromCodeCoverage: text only; 2 agent test(s) linked to no criterion

findings.title: The #if guard excludes netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework although the attribute exists there
findings.verification_note: Attribute present in netstandard.dll (2.0.3) and System.dll (net472). Small factual error by the AI: it placed it in mscorlib.

findings.title: Unrequested change in the nested-type emitter
findings.verification_note: Necessary change: an #if must start a line. Only one snapshot affected (HasPrivateSerializedMemberAndIsGenericNamed). Not declared by the agent → orphan.

findings.title: The test checks one substring per file, not each type, and compiles nothing
findings.verification_note: The test also encodes C2's false premise as expected behaviour.

findings.title: Possible CS0579 if the user's partial resolver already carries the attribute
findings.also_stated: [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] on a partial class is fine
findings.verification_note: CS0579 reproduced: compilation regression for these users. The AI had rated it low / confidence 0.4.

missed_by_ai.what: Code written by hand in a user's partial resolver is excluded from coverage
missed_by_ai.note: The AI even stated: “[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] on a partial class is fine”.
